client_brief:
Performer laminates for Lanternwood, rebuilt from last year's printed artwork

Twenty-two people need correct performer laminates. Our designer left in 2024, and the usable starting point is last year's printed artwork. We need a production designer who will rebuild the run carefully, not carry last year's names or fields into new passes.

Passes
Twenty two laminates built off last year's printed artwork: one press file the printer can run with one person per page and page count equal to roster count, plus twenty two separate single passes named to the roster, plus proofs at true print-resolution sized to the pass trim. Every field carries that person's own value, nothing is inherited from last year's text, no record truncates at trim, and the role colour coding is one reconciled scheme.

Festival photographs
The fourteen archive frames brought to one festival target, one white point, one black point, one crop logic, with a per-frame parameter log and a line on why any frame differs from its neighbours, plus one licensed camera-scale field frame graded into the same world. Frames that cannot be brought to the set are named. The reconciliation of frames against approved billing is delivered with the set, including which billed act the archive does not cover.

Please reconcile the role colours into one scheme and check every pass at its actual trim. The archive photographs also need comparing with the approved billing: a folder of fourteen frames does not necessarily mean fourteen different billed acts are covered.

The supplied materials are lanternwood_pass_2026.pdf; lanternwood_roster_2027.csv; lanternwood_banner_mainstage.jpg; lanternwood_stage_frames/ (14 frames, camera scale); lanternwood_lineup_2027.txt; lanternwood_site_plan_pencil.png.

We need individual files that are correctly named and a combined printer file whose page count matches the roster. Please identify any photograph you cannot bring into the shared festival look.

This is a fixed-price commission at $3,000-$7,000, with a target of 2 to 4 weeks. The agreed review allowance is one direction checkpoint and two consolidated revision rounds. New deliverable classes, new source creation, extra records, and client copy changes after approval are quoted separately.

Alongside the finished work, we need a delivery manifest, the editable sources specified above, final exports, a short production and exceptions note and the normalised data and field-mapping record. Keep a clear record of the supplied files used, retained for reference, superseded and rejected. Approved source information remains authoritative. Record omissions, substitutions, reconciliations and quality limits, and do not use an undeclared replacement or invented fact to conceal a source problem.

source_provenance.statement: The scenario is synthesized from the repository's laundered Upwork and Freelancer source anchors. It is not represented as a verbatim live listing.
source_provenance.original_anchor: Primary anchor: the Upwork event credential post quoted in the ledger's grounding_note, an events team wanting personalised backstage and performer passes produced from a lineup list against a designer built page layout template, delivered both as one file the printer can run and as separate passes to send out. Co anchor: the second Upwork post in the ledger, whose literal ask was to BUILD a page layout plugin that automatically reduces font sizes when a record is too long for its frame, because merged text runs overset and get clipped on export. That second post is a software commission and is out of scope for any design connector, but the PAIN it names is real, it is the single most common failure of a variable data print run, and this engagement makes the agent meet it by hand rather than automate it away. Both real posts name a client nowhere, so the line is laundered to the coined fictional festival Lanternwood Folk Fest; every performer, crew member, stage and sponsor name is invented and no real festival, venue, act or trademark appears in any task facing field. The ledger's repositioning note killed the original because it merged into a convert_pdf_to_indd output and relied on a per row data merge image field that cannot exist in a converted PDF. CONNECTOR_CAPABILITIES_v3 (2026-09-10) changes what the honest fuller commission is: the convert, prepare, merge chain IS verified to bind fields end to end off a bare press PDF, provided the mapping offsets are computed from the true interchange story rather than from the tool's own readout, while the per row image field genuinely does not exist unless the source PDF carried a real placed image. So the corrected commission keeps the client's actual pass run and makes both of those realities load bearing, and it adds the rest of the kit that client obviously needed at the same on sale date.

price_band_and_audience: Mid tier independent festival. Weekend general admission a hundred and forty five dollars, VIP three hundred and twenty, roughly four thousand weekend tickets, audience eighteen to forty, discovery led and scene literate rather than corporate. The band is load bearing in both directions. Push sparse and luxurious, with acres of white, a hairline serif and one small photograph, and it reads as a three hundred and twenty dollar tasting event rather than a farm field weekend, which suppresses general admission conversion where nearly all the revenue sits. Push the other way into a dense bargain flyer, with every act at the same size, a starburst price and clip art, and the VIP tier stops being credible and the discovery stages read as filler. The correct register is energetic and coherent: bold type at a real hierarchy, atmospheric photography carrying the field and the night, a lineup that plainly distinguishes headline from discovery, and colour coding a gate steward reads at two metres in daylight. A posted commission of this shape and scope runs 1,800 to 3,500 dollars fixed.

assets_supplied.name: lanternwood_pass_2026.pdf
assets_supplied.kind: Last year's performer laminate artwork, the press PDF the printer returned, portrait, one pass per page, with a photo box, a name block, an act line, a role bar and a stage and day strip.
assets_supplied.visible_description: "Last year's pass, exactly as the printer sent it back. Same shape this year, new colours, new names."
assets_supplied.hidden_defect: The five blocks that read as separate fields on the printed page are one continuous text flow once converted, so there is nothing to map field by field, and the readout used to build a mapping silently omits the low contrast handle run while keeping its line break, which leaves every offset past it short by exactly that run while the validator still answers VALID and the prepare step still answers completed successfully. The photo box is drawn artwork rather than a placed image, so no graphic frame exists for a per performer headshot to bind to, and nothing in the printed page or the file listing says so.

assets_supplied.name: lanternwood_roster_2027.csv
assets_supplied.kind: Twenty two rows: person, act, role, stages cleared, days on site, social handle, and a column of headshot filenames.
assets_supplied.visible_description: "Everyone who wears a laminate. It is final apart from one crew name we are still confirming."
assets_supplied.hidden_defect: Several act strings run long (a duo billed with a guest brass section, one act carrying a parenthetical subtitle) and the pass measure does not overset visibly, it simply stops rendering at the frame edge, so the merge succeeds, the page count still equals the row count and the record reads as complete until the trim is examined. Role values arrive in three different spellings and cases across the twenty two rows, and the colour coding the client wants is keyed to them.

assets_supplied.name: lanternwood_banner_mainstage.jpg
assets_supplied.kind: Handheld photograph of the painted canvas banner over the main stage, carrying the festival mark: a lantern with cut window panes, sitting inside a ring of small caps type, over a hand painted rule.
assets_supplied.visible_description: "The only place our mark still exists since the drive went. It has hung there since 2022."
assets_supplied.hidden_defect: The trace comes back clean and convincing at canvas size, but the lantern's window panes and the counters inside the ring close up at the size the mark actually reproduces in the announcement set corner lockup and the site plan legend, on the dark ground those two sit on, and nothing reports it because the trace itself succeeded. The banner's right third hangs in shade where the painted ink and the canvas run close in value, so a selection worded for the ink alone comes back short on that side.

assets_supplied.name: lanternwood_stage_frames/ (14 frames, camera scale)
assets_supplied.kind: Last year's performance photography, shot by two volunteers on two different bodies across the three stages, mixed daylight, dusk and stage light.
assets_supplied.visible_description: "Everything we have from last year. Some of it is lovely. It was two people with two cameras and no brief."
assets_supplied.hidden_defect: Three of the fourteen are the same act photographed on the same night from three positions, and one of the three 2027 headliners appears in none of the fourteen at all, which no filename, caption or column reveals and which only surfaces when the frames are read against the billing. Two frames were shot into the low sun and sit a full stop hotter than the rest of the set.

emergent_checkpoints.what_can_only_be_learned_by_running: What last year's pass actually becomes once it is a working document, and whether a mapping the tools blessed actually landed. The printed page shows five clearly separated blocks; the converted document can expose them as a single continuous text flow with no addressable per field frames, and the photo box that reads as a picture frame on paper can convert as drawn artwork with no graphic frame at all, which removes the per performer headshot binding the roster's filename column was written for. On top of that, the readout used to compute the mapping can silently omit a low contrast run while keeping its line break, so the string still looks well formed and every offset past the omission is short by exactly that run. The validator answers VALID with no warnings and the prepare step answers completed successfully, and only a placeholder inventory taken back out of the document reveals that some fields never landed.
emergent_checkpoints.why_unavoidable: Ordering cannot dodge it because the granularity of a converted PDF is a property of the source artwork and is not exposed until the conversion has been run and the document read back. Nothing in the brief, the file listing or the printed page states any of it: the client believes the pass is five fields and a photo box, which is what it looks like. The response is not a re run of the same chain, it is a different mapping strategy entirely, offsets computed inside one story against a reconstructed text, plus a decision about what to do with a headshot that now has nowhere to go.
emergent_checkpoints.likely_rework: Rebuild the mapping from a reconstructed story text rather than the readout, re prepare the template, re verify the placeholder inventory field by field, and re plan the headshot: either carry it as part of the delivered artwork by another route or tell the client plainly that this year's pass cannot carry a photo from this source.
emergent_checkpoints.failure_if_undetected: A twenty two page run that assembles cleanly and prints with several fields blank or still carrying last year's artwork text, discovered by a gate steward on the first morning of a festival that has already been laminated.

emergent_checkpoints.what_can_only_be_learned_by_running: Whether every record survives the frame it landed in. The pass measure is fixed, and a string longer than the measure does not overset visibly and does not raise a warning: it simply stops rendering at the frame edge, so the record looks complete, the run reports success and the page count still equals the row count. Which of the twenty two this happens to is a function of each act's own billing string against the inherited frame width, and no column, no count and no response says which.
emergent_checkpoints.why_unavoidable: There is no ordering that avoids it and no parameter that prevents it, because the frame width is inherited from artwork the client supplied rather than chosen. Nothing states it either: the brief says the roster is final and lists what each pass must carry, and the acceptance line about nothing truncating is the printer's standing requirement, not a disclosure that a particular act is too long. And the response is not a re merge of the same thing, it is a craft decision per affected record about measure, about how the act line is set, or about what abbreviates without misbilling an act.
emergent_checkpoints.likely_rework: Read every page of the proof at trim rather than the run summary, identify the records that stop short, change the way the act and stage strings are set for the whole run so one rule covers all twenty two, then re merge, re render and re read.
emergent_checkpoints.failure_if_undetected: Laminates printed and heat sealed with an act billed as half its own name and a performer cleared for stages the pass does not show, on the one artefact that cannot be corrected after it is made.

emergent_checkpoints.what_can_only_be_learned_by_running: Whether the recovered mark still holds where it is smallest. The trace off the painted banner comes back clean, complete and convincing at canvas size, and it sits well at poster scale. At the size it actually reproduces in the announcement set corner lockup and in the site plan legend, over the dark ground both of those sit on, the lantern's window panes and the counters inside the type ring can close and fill in, and the hand painted rule can thicken into the ring. Nothing reports it, because the trace succeeded, the vector is valid and the placement is correct.
emergent_checkpoints.why_unavoidable: No ordering avoids it, because the reproduction size and the ground only exist once the canvases are composed, and no measurement is available anywhere in the connector to predict it. Nothing states it: the brief asks for the mark back as artwork for the posters, the announcement set and the programme, and never asks how small it can go. The response is not a re export, it is a different raster preparation upstream, a selection weighted to the paint body rather than to its edges, or a plate filled and traced at a different polarity, producing a second mark drawn for small use.
emergent_checkpoints.likely_rework: Prepare and trace a small use variant of the mark from the banner by a different route, judge it at true reproduction size on the actual dark ground rather than on canvas, re place it in the announcement set and the legend, re export, and record the two variants and their intended sizes in the basis page and the note.
emergent_checkpoints.failure_if_undetected: An announcement set going out on the on sale morning to four thousand ticket buyers with the festival's mark reduced to a dark blob in the corner, and a programme legend where the lantern has no windows.

decision_gates: Which deliverables are a record per page variable data run and which need an authored fixed canvas document, given that only one surface here composes free form layout at all.
Whether to trust the mapping readout or to reconstruct the template's true story text before computing a single offset.
What to do about a headshot column written for a photo box that turns out not to be a photo box.
How the act and stage strings are set across the whole run so that one rule keeps all twenty two records whole, rather than patching the records that happen to fail.
How far to push the two into the sun frames before they stop being worth saving, versus naming them.
Whether fourteen archive frames covers a three headliner billing, and how to say so when it does not.

Selection wording on the painted banner: naming the substrate takes the canvas, naming the paint's own visual properties takes the mark, and background removal on an enclosed ring is the wrong instrument entirely.
Which mark variant carries which canvas, judged at reproduction size on the actual ground rather than at canvas size.

why_not_vlm: Paste the brief and the assets into a frontier image model and it returns a handsome picture of a folk festival poster. IDENTITY: the mark has to be RECOVERED off a photograph of the actual painted banner that has hung over the main stage since 2022, because a regenerated lantern is a different festival's logo, and the photography has to be of the acts who are actually billed. SPEC: twenty two laminates, one person per page, each carrying that person's own name, act, role, stages and days, printed at trim by a printer who cannot fix a truncated act name afterwards, plus separate single files named to the roster. A generated image satisfies none of that and cannot be checked for any of it. EDITABILITY: the client says outright that acts will move through the winter and they will be changing the announcement set themselves, so the deliverable is defined by being a document they can open and retype. And the middle of this engagement is verification against material reality: what the converted pass actually contains, whether the mapping the validator blessed actually landed, whether this record survived its frame, whether the mark holds at the size it reproduces.
